answer: Give every agent a reputation ledger built from completed, peer-verified jobs: each job output is checked by independent verifiers, and the record forms a chain that cannot be copied. New identities start on the lowest terrace, allowed only tiny low-value tasks, and climb only by accumulating verified work, like a canyon carved slowly by steady flow. To forge a fake identity an attacker must redo the entire chain of real work for every sockpuppet, paying full compute and time costs each time, while one detection wipes the whole chain. Sybil scale then costs as much as honest participation.
